lead: Amazon rose 3.96% on Black Friday's half-day session after early holiday data came in strong: Adobe said US Thanksgiving Day online spending hit $7.1 billion, up 10.4% from last year and above its $6.9 billion forecast.
why: Holiday spending: the Motley Fool tied the rise to 'encouraging early Black Friday shopping data'. Adobe Analytics: Thanksgiving online $7.1B (+10.4% y/y, vs $6.9B forecast); Nov 1-22 online $82.5B (+9.1%) vs a 6.7% full-season forecast of $275.1B; forecasts Black Friday $12.9B (+9.2%), Cyber Monday $15.1B, Cyber Week $47.5B (GuruFocus via TradingView). Adobe counts all US online stores, not Amazon alone.

Amazon share of wallet and AI: Numerator survey says 87% of Cyber Weekend shoppers plan to buy on Amazon (Walmart 65%, Target 42%); Goldman kept AMZN on its Conviction List, $370 target (Finexus). SemiAnalysis posted (Nov 26) that Trainium3 UltraServer showed 2.28x better perf per dollar than Nvidia GB300 NVL72 in its agentic inference benchmark (KuCoin/Benzinga Pro). Next: Cyber Monday and AWS re:Invent both start Nov 30.

Market: S&P 500 +1.60% (7,297.49), Nasdaq +2.31% (24,129.50), Dow +1.18% (50,774.94); best week in 19 months as AI stocks rebounded (Motley Fool). Tesla about +5% after a German antitrust filing showed plans to buy automation maker EMAG (JournalArta, intraday). Micron +7.6%, Sandisk ~+16% (chips, @5beforemonday). Revised Q3 GDP +4.3%.
